EXPLANATION: Strong, sharp C–H stretching cluster at 2880–2970 cm⁻¹ (typical of saturated aliphatic C-H in tertiary amines).  A distinct band at 2804 cm⁻¹ matches the characteristic N-CH₃/CH₂ stretch of trialkylamines.  Intense CH₃/CH₂ deformation at 1458 cm⁻¹ and methyl rock at 741 cm⁻¹ fit ethyl groups.  The 1070–1090 cm⁻¹ doublet and bands at 1003/1023 cm⁻¹ correspond to C–C / C–N skeletal stretches and CH₃ rocking seen in triethylamine spectra.  Absence of O–H (∼3300 cm⁻¹) or C=O/C≡C features rules out alcohol/ether or unsaturated candidates.  Overall pattern best matches the simple trialkylamine CCN(CC)CC (triethylamine).
